input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 14 gives Client an unconditional election to terminate the Agreement on written notice, with service continuing only until the last day of the month following notice (roughly 30–60 days). That is a Customer convenience right no more onerous than the 60–90 days' notice contemplated at the fallback, and no early-termination fee or penalty is imposed anywhere (Section 5 bills monthly in arrears against invoices paid within 15 days of receipt), so the fee cap element is satisfied a fortiori. On the Vendor side there is no mid-term convenience right at all: Section 13 lets Sections 2 and 3 fall away only for Client breach/default (a for-cause trigger), and TrueLink's only other exit is a notice of intent not to renew at the end of the one-year term, which is a natural-term non-renewal question under RENEWAL (30 days' notice) rather than a T4C convenience termination, so we do not flag it twice here. The bargain therefore sits at or above the fallback and we would not redline it. Two points short of the preferred wording are noted for information only, not as deviations: the notice mechanic can run past 30 days where notice is given early in a month, and there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (of limited practical effect given monthly arrears invoicing).
